rows.name: WORLD x-y death card (the black card shown between lives)
rows.notes: Black death/respawn card. Top status bar (nametable 0 rows 2-3) stays unchanged: MARIO 000200, coin x01, WORLD 1-1, and the TIME label with its three digit cells blank ($24). Card content: the words 'WORLD 1-1' on nametable row 10 (pixels y 80-87) at cols 11-19 = $20 W, $18 O, $1B R, $15 L, $0D D, blank $24, $01 digit 1, $28 dash, $01 digit 1; a small Mario sprite; and a lives line on row 14 (y 112-119): tile $29 'x' at col 15 and a digit at col 18. Everything is drawn from BACKGROUND PATTERN TABLE $1000 - nametable tile ids $00-$FF map to CHR $100-$1FF (verified: card 'O' tile_id 24 = CHR $118, card '1' tile_id 1 = CHR $101, lives '5' tile_id 5 = CHR $105). PALETTES (live PPU palette RAM read while paused): the black field is NOT a tile - the blank tile $24 is CHR $124, an all-index-0 (transparent) tile, so the whole screen is the shared backdrop PPU $3F00 = $0F black (live palette RAM byte 0 = $0F; note get_all_palettes reported palette 0 slot 0 as $22 periwinkle here, which did not match live palette RAM). BG palette 2 [$0F,$30 white,$21 sky blue,$1C teal] paints ALL the card text and the lives digit through slot 1 = $30 white ('WORLD 1-1' sampled white at (104,85); the 'x' at (122,117) white; tile attribute blocks for the text are palette 2). The two blank tiles at row 14 cols 16-17 sit in a palette-3 attribute block but are transparent. Small Mario is a SPRITE, not background: list_sprites decodes the standard 8-entry small-Mario metasprite (4 blank $FC filler + tiles $3A,$37 at y105 and $4F,$4F-hflip at y113) at origin (96,89), visible box (96,105)-(111,120), sprite palette 4 = [$0F,$16 red,$27 orange,$18 olive]. The lives digit shows the lives counter $075A plus one: while the card was up, RAM $075A read 4 and the card showed '5' (an earlier identical card showed '3' when $075A read 2).
rows.why: the black card 'WORLD 1-1' with Mario x 5 over the fixed HUD, taken paused right after a lost life, as the reach says

rows.name: World 1-2 (underground, opening screen)
rows.notes: World 1-2, the underground level, first screen (camera x=0, Mario at the bottom-left). Everything visible is BACKGROUND: nametable 0, BACKGROUND PATTERN TABLE $1000 (every nametable tile id $00-$FF draws CHR $100-$1FF; verified: brick tile_id 71 = CHR $147, ? block bottom-right tile_id 86 = CHR $156, blank tile_id 36 = CHR $124). Layout: a black cave with a brick ceiling along the top, a brick floor along the bottom, a row of four 16x16 ? blocks mid-screen around y 152 (tile ids $53/$54 top and $55/$56 bottom - the same ? block graphic as World 1-1), and two walking Goombas on the right. WHICH PALETTE PAINTS WHAT (live PPU palette RAM read while paused): BG palette 0 = [$0F black, $29 lime green, $1A green, $09 dark green]; its slot 0 $0F black IS the shared backdrop (PPU $3F00) that fills the whole cave - the blank tile $24 (CHR $124) is all-index-0, so every empty cell shows the backdrop black, and slots 1-3 ($29/$1A/$09 greens) are the pipe/scenery greens used later in the level (no pipe on this first screen). BG palette 1 = [$0F, $3C pale cyan, $1C teal, $0F] paints the CAVE BRICKS of the ceiling, walls and floor: the wall brick sampled at (12,120) is nametable tile $47 / palette 1 / CHR $147 and renders $1C teal (rgb 0,124,141); slot 2 $1C teal is the brick body, slot 1 $3C pale cyan the highlight and slot 3 $0F black the mortar. Palette 2 = [$0F, $30 white, $21 sky blue, $1C teal] paints the fixed HUD text (slot 1 $30 white) exactly as in the overworld. Palette 3 = [$0F, $17 brown, $17 brown, $1C teal] paints the ? BLOCKS: get_tile_at_pixel (170,156) returns tile_id 86 ($56) / palette 3 / CHR $156 and renders $17 brown with a $1C teal edge - so in 1-2 the ? blocks are brown/teal, not the overworld orange. Sprite palette 4 = [$0F, $16 red, $27 orange, $18 olive] = Mario; sprite palette 7 = [$0F, $0C dark teal, $3C pale cyan, $1C teal] paints the two Goombas (list_sprites: two 16x24 metasprites, OAM slots 12-17 and 18-23, tiles $70-$73, attr $43 -> palette 7), which is why underground Goombas are blue-teal. The area palette chain confirmed: header index $0760=2 -> $0750=$C0 -> $074E=2 -> $85BB[2]=3 -> the selector-3 palette block at prgRom 0xCEC ($8CEC); the live palette RAM matches that block.
rows.why: HUD reads WORLD 1-2; black backdrop, blue-green brick ceiling, wall and floor, the row of ? blocks and two Goombas in the underground palette: World 1-2's opening, reached by writing the area index before Start

rows.name: level/area index that selects which area the game loads
rows.notes: This is how the game picks the area it loads, proven in the emulator. The level-init area selector at CPU $9C00-$9C12 (prgRom 0x1C00) does JSR $9C13, where $9C13: LDY $075F (world) / LDA $9CB4,Y (world base table = 0,5,10,14,19,23,27,32 for worlds 1-8) / CLC / ADC $0760 / TAY / LDA $9CBC,Y (level-header table) / RTS. The returned header is stored to $0750 at $9C06; then $9C09-$9C0F derives the palette group with (header & $60) << 1 as a 4x ROL, storing $074E, and LoadAreaData ($9C22-$9C2E) sets $074F = header & $1F. The layout pointer is $9D28[$074E] + $074F indexing the low/high tables $9D2C/$9D4E; the enemy pointer is $9CE0[$074E] + $074F indexing $9CE4/$9D06. For World 1 ($075F=0, base 0) the header index = $0760: index 0 -> header $25 -> $074E=1, $074F=5 -> World 1-1 (layout $A68E); index 2 -> header $C0 -> $074E=2 (underground), $074F=0 -> World 1-2 (layout header $AC35, records $AC37). $074E selects the palette block through $85BB = $01,$02,$03,$04: $074E=0 -> selector 1 $8CA4, 1 -> selector 2 $8CC8 (overworld), 2 -> selector 3 $8CEC (underground, black cave + $1C teal bricks), 3 -> selector 4 $8D10 (castle grayscale). PROOF: with $075F=0, writing $0760=1 on the title and starting gave $074E=1/$074F=9 (an overworld-looking area at layout $A832); writing $0760=2 gave $074E=2/$074F=0/$0750=$C0 and World 1-2's black underground screen with layout pointer $00E7/$00E8=$AC37 (see the 'underground' scene). Death reloads do NOT re-run this selector - they reuse the latched $074E/$074F - so the write must happen before Start (or before the next-level transition), not on the WORLD x-y card.

rows.name: World 2-2 (under water, opening screen)
rows.notes: World 2-2, the under-water level, first screen. Mario stands at the bottom-left in water; everything else visible is BACKGROUND: nametable 0, BACKGROUND PATTERN TABLE $1000 (get_tile_at_pixel reports background_pattern_addr 4096 on every BG pixel; nametable tile $26 = CHR $126, tile $85 = CHR $185). Screen contents: fixed top HUD (MARIO 000000, coin x00, WORLD 2-2, TIME 396), a mid-screen cloud-like cluster of bubbles, a tall pink coral at x~176-191, and a green kelp/seaweed floor across the bottom with two dark-brown coral metatiles at the right edge. WHICH PALETTE PAINTS WHAT (live palette RAM read while paused): BG palette 0 = [$22 periwinkle, $15 magenta, $12 bright blue, $25 pink]: slot 0 $22 is the shared backdrop (PPU $3F00) and shows as the lighter periwinkle band behind the HUD top rows (get_pixel_color(40,25) = $22) and wherever the blank tile $24 appears; slots 1-3 paint the PINK CORAL decoration (get_region object mode at (181,190) = 768 connected background palette-0 pixels using slots 1,2,3, box (176,160)-(191,207), CHR 0x1A4/0x1E9/0x1EA/0x1EB; the leaf face renders $25 pink, get_pixel_color(181,190)). BG palette 1 = [$0F, $3A pale green, $1A green, $0F] paints the KELP/SEAWEED FLOOR: the floor metatile is tiles $82/$84 (top row) over $83/$85 (bottom row); get_tile_at_pixel(40,232) = tile_id 133 ($85) / palette 1 / CHR $185 and renders $1A green, while the lighter tile $84 sampled at (250,208) renders $3A pale green, and slot 3 $0F is the black outline. BG palette 2 = [$0F, $30 white, $12 bright blue, $0F] does double duty: its slot 2 $12 bright blue paints the WATER BODY - the whole playfield is filled with tile $26 (CHR $126, all pixel index 2), and get_region color mode at (100,150) selected 4096 pixels of palette-2 slot 2 across CHR 0x126 filling the screen - while its slot 1 $30 white paints ALL the fixed HUD text/digits (e.g. the WORLD '2' at (152,24) is tile_id 2 / palette 2, sampled white $30). BG palette 3 = [$0F, $07 dark brown, $12 bright blue, $0F] paints the dark CORAL/ROCK metatile at the right edge: nametable cols 28-31 rows 24-25 hold tiles $C2/$C3 (row 24) and $C4/$C5 (row 25), and get_tile_at_pixel(246,204) = tile_id 196 ($C4) / palette 3 / CHR $1C4, rendered $07 dark brown; slot 2 $12 is not visible in view. SPRITES: sprite palette 4 = [$22, $16 red, $27 orange, $18 olive] is small Mario (list_sprites: tiles $3A,$37,$4F at origin (40,177)); sprite palette 6 = [$0F, $16 red, $30 white, $27 orange] draws Mario's rising BUBBLES (three OAM entries, tile $74, x=49, y=140/158/178); sprite palette 7 = [$0F, $0F, $30 white, $16 red] is the behind-background HUD coin sprite $FF at (88,25). The area palette chain confirmed: world 2 base 5 + $0760=2 -> header index 7 = $9CBC[7] = $01 -> $074E=0 -> selector table $85BB[0] = 1 -> the water palette block at prgRom 0x8CA4 ($8CA4), and the live palette RAM matches that block.
rows.why: HUD reads WORLD 2-2; blue water backdrop with the wave line at the top, green coral floor, pink coral and bubbles: World 2-2's opening

rows.name: World 1-4 (castle, opening screen)
rows.notes: World 1-4, the castle level, first screen (camera x=0, small Mario on the left ledge). Everything visible except Mario is BACKGROUND: nametable 0, BACKGROUND PATTERN TABLE $1000 (get_tile_at_pixel reports background_pattern_addr 4096 on every BG pixel; nametable tile $5D = CHR $15D, $5E = CHR $15E, $41 = CHR $141, $26 = CHR $126, blank $24 = CHR $124). Screen contents: fixed top HUD (MARIO 000000, coin x00, WORLD 1-4, TIME 294), a black backdrop, gray castle-brick walls/floor (metatile = tile $5D on each even row over $5E on the next row), and a fire/lava column at the bottom-right that reaches up into the blackness. The lava/spike column tiles in the red area lit as a continuous red mass across CHR 0x126/0x141. WHICH PALETTE PAINTS WHAT (live palette RAM read while paused): BG palette 0 = [$0F black, $30 white, $10 gray, $00 dark gray]: slot 0 $0F is the shared backdrop (PPU $3F00) and IS the black background that fills the screen (the blank tile $24/CHR $124 is all pixel index 0; get_pixel_color(200,80) = $0F black, and the blank cells are nametable tile_id 36); its other slots are not visible on this screen. BG palette 1 = [$0F, $30 white, $10 gray, $00 dark gray] paints the CASTLE BRICK WALLS AND FLOOR: the brick metatile is tile $5D (nametable id 93, CHR $15D) on the top row and $5E (nametable id 94, CHR $15E) on the row below (read_nametable 0 at (0,14): row14 = 5D x6, row15 = 5E x6); get_tile_at_pixel(10,120) = tile_id 94 / palette 1 / CHR $15E, get_region object mode there = palette 1, slots 1-3, CHR 0x15E; slot 1 $30 white is the brick highlight (sampled white at (10,120) and (60,180)), slot 2 $10 gray the midtone, slot 3 $00 dark gray the body/shadow (sampled dark gray at (14,124)). BG palette 2 = [$0F, $30 white, $16 red, $00 dark gray] does double duty: its slot 2 $16 red paints the LAVA/FIRE column at the bottom-right - nametable cols 28-29 rows 24-26 hold tile $41 (flame, nametable id 65, CHR $141) over tile $26 (solid fill, nametable id 38, CHR $126); get_region color mode at (228,210) selected 1396 pixels of palette-2 slot 2 across CHR 0x126/0x141, box (208,193)-(239,239), all rendering $16 red (get_pixel_color(225,215) = $16) - while its slot 1 $30 white paints ALL the fixed HUD text/digits (get_pixel_color at (156,25) on the WORLD '1' stroke = $30 white; the HUD '1' is tile_id 1 / palette 2). Slot 3 $00 is not used by the lava. BG palette 3 = [$0F, $17 brown, $17 brown, $00 dark gray]: NOT visible on the opening screen (the brown slots are used later in the castle). SPRITES: sprite palette 4 = [$0F, $16 red, $27 orange, $18 olive] is small Mario (list_sprites: 8-entry small-Mario metasprite at origin (40,81), tiles $3A/$37 and $4F/$4F-hflip); sprite palette 7 = [$0F, $00 dark gray, $30 white, $16 red] is the behind-background HUD coin sprite $FF at (88,25). No Firebar (bar of fireballs) or other enemy sprite is present on this first screen; list_sprites returned only Mario plus the HUD coin sprite. The area palette chain confirmed: world 1 base 0 + $0760=4 -> header index 4 = $9CBC[4] = $60 -> $074E = ($60 >> 5) & 3 = 3 (castle area type), $074F = $60 & $1F = 0 -> selector table $85BB[3] = 4 -> the castle palette block at prgRom 0x8D10 ($8D10), and the live palette RAM matches that block.
rows.why: HUD reads WORLD 1-4; gray castle brick ceiling, steps and floor on black, a lava pit at the right: World 1-4's opening
